overview: A two-mode cosmetic held-item animation switcher: on every UpdateEvent it writes a static int — 1 for the '1.7' mode, 6 for the 'Sigma' mode — that the client's render path reads to change the swing/held-item pose. It sends no packets; the vanilla C0APacketAnimation swing stream continues unchanged, so swing-packet anticheats observe an identical stream.

sections.p: The module's entire state is a public static int anim. The single UpdateEvent consumer sets it to 1 or 6 depending on which of the two modes (1.7, Sigma) is selected; any render or animation code elsewhere in the client reads Animations.anim to choose its pose. There is no per-tick work beyond the assignment, no onEnable/onDisable logic, and no packet interaction.

C0APacketAnimation is emitted by the vanilla swing path (attacks, block interactions, right-clicks) through EntityPlayer.swingItem, independently of how the held item is rendered. Because the module only changes the client-side pose, the C0A stream the server receives is byte-identical to vanilla. The real anticheat surface for animation cheats is therefore not this module but the adjacent class that does alter the swing stream — killaura that attacks without swinging (caught by NoSwing checks) and autoclickers that flood swings (caught by swing-frequency checks).

files.label: Animations.java
files.explanation: A static int plus one consumer. The UpdateEvent handler compares the active mode by name and writes the matching animation id into the shared static, which is the entire public contract of the module — other Nekoware render code switches its pose off Animations.anim, so toggling the module changes the visual without any per-frame cost or any packet. The mode check is exclusive: with 1.7 selected the value is 1, with Sigma it is 6, and no other value is ever written.

countering.label: NoSwing (arm-swing requirement between attacks)
countering.explanation: NCP's fight NoSwing enforces that the player moves their arm between attacks: an attack event runs NoSwing.check, and a preceding swing (C0A) rewards a decay of noSwingVL (x0.9), while an attack with no preceding swing accumulates noSwingCount and raises noSwingVL by 1 per attack, executing the configured actions when the level passes the threshold. Honest note: this module never suppresses C0A — the vanilla swing still fires on every attack — so the check stays satisfied and cannot see the pose change. It is the real detector for the animation-cheat class this module's feature sits next to (killaura attacking without arm swings), and the mechanism it relies on is exactly the C0A stream the module leaves intact.

countering.label: NoSwing (combat, legacy swing-time window)
countering.explanation: Arc's combat NoSwing times swings against attacks. On 1.8 it runs the legacy branch: after an attack, if the time since the last swing packet exceeds max-swing-time-old (default 100ms), it fails with 'No swing animation within time'. On newer versions the check only fires when an attack landed within the last second and the swing gap still exceeds the allowed window, which avoids flagging idle players. Honest note: the check measures the C0A stream relative to attacks; Nekoware's Animations alters neither, so a player using it passes. It is the closest real swing-stream check in Arc and represents the timing-based approach to the same cheat class.

countering.label: SwingFrequency (swing packet rate)
countering.explanation: Arc's swing flood detector: a scheduled task runs every 20 ticks, counts the player's swing packets for the second, and flags 'Too many swing packets per second' once the count reaches maxPacketsPerSecond (default 50), with an optional hard kick at packetKickThreshold (default 100) and a cancel path that drops subsequent swings while flagged. This catches autoclicker and animation-spam clients that flood C0A. Honest note: the module emits zero extra swings — the client's swing rate is unchanged — so the per-second count never approaches the cap; the check is the real detector for the flood side of the animation-packet axis this module does not touch.

countering.label: NoSwingBreak (break without swing)
countering.explanation: Grim's breaking variant of the no-swing family: it latches sentBreak on any non-cancelled digging action and sentAnimation on any ANIMATION packet, and at each tick boundary flags if a break was sent without a swing in the same tick, resetting both latches. It targets clients that mine with packet-level speed hacks while suppressing the arm animation. Honest note: the module leaves the vanilla swing path intact, so every break still carries its C0A and the latches always pair; it is the per-tick swing-consistency check that would catch the suppression cheat this module's feature class is commonly paired with.
